messages:
lee: heads-up: we got flaky auth failures in localtest when multiple redwoodctl instances start while the background self-updater is running. mac + linux.
priya: what do the failures look like?
dan: paste of a real failure from a runner: 
`Error: login failed: 401 unauthorized - helper: no token returned`
lee: repro: spawn 4 parallel `redwoodctl login --headless --profile=ci-test` in same $USER. ~12% of runs return that 401 when updater is active.
taylor: could be a profile merge that clobbers the currently used credential file during swap. any file ops in updater?
lee: yes updater writes a new binary and moves over, and we also have a small migration step that copies legacy profiles into ~/.redwood/profiles.json; during that copy the file briefly has 644 perms and then we chmod back. concurrent helpers sometimes read midway.
priya: quick mitigation: add an optimistic retry in the credential helper when token is empty (small backoff + jitter). also make helper check for in-progress updater via presence of `.updater.lock` and wait a bit.
dan: agree. long-term fix: updater should write to a temp path and then mv into place without touching profiles.json or use a config-lock. also make profile migration run only once on cold-start, not during binary swap.
lee: I added a tiny harness `test/local-login-race --parallel 4 --loops 100` that reproduces. putting logs in a gist.
taylor: (typo) taylor: CI suggestion: add a nightly canary that runs the harness after each updater build so we catch regressions.
ci-bot: Canary job created: canary/local-login-race (runs nightly).
priya: filing PRs: 1) helper-retry hotfix (configurable via REDWOODCTL_AUTH_RETRIES), 2) updater-migration-lock (follow-up). will include harness and failure rates.
dan: timeline ok for hotfix today, updater rollback next week. thumbs up from me.
lee: thanks. I'll include notes in the release notes and an opt-out env var REDWOODCTL_DISABLE_SELFUPDATE for devs running localtest.
priya: perfect.
